newsitem.title: USA: NO SIGN CANADA TO LIMIT WHEAT SHIPMENTS-US'S DALEY.
newsitem.headline: NO SIGN CANADA TO LIMIT WHEAT SHIPMENTS-US'S DALEY.

text.p: Canadian officials gave no indication they would curb wheat shipments into the U.S. market, U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley said Thursday at the end of a three-day trade mission.
Speaking to reporters by telephone from Vancouver, Daley said, "No, they did not" when asked if Canadian officials said they would back off on sales to U.S. buyers.
Farmers and lawmakers from the Wheat Belt contend Canadian wheat has driven down U.S. prices. Some want a halt to all Canadia grain shipments.
The Clinton administration was looking at options to restrain shipments, including a review by the Commerce Department whether an antidumping investigation was warranted.
Daley declined to suggest when the department would complete its initial survey, saying, "We have a lot of information-gathering to do.
"That's a decision to be made after you gather information," Daley said when asked if the department might self-initiate an antidumping investigation.
